chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us. He said: Salama ibn al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Tasnim al-Warraq narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir from his father from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions one day: O my companions!

Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — commands you to the wilaya of Ali ibn Abi Talib and to follow his example. He is your master and your Imam after me. Do not oppose him, lest you disbelieve; and do not separate from him, lest you go astray. Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — has made Ali a sign distinguishing between faith and hypocrisy: whoever loves him is a believer, and whoever hates him is a hypocrite.

Indeed, God — Mighty is His Majesty — has made Ali my designated successor, the beacon of guidance after me, the repository of my secret, the treasury of my knowledge, and my vicegerent among my family. I complain to God about those from my nation who will oppress him after me.

key_terms.جل جلاله: Mighty is His Majesty; a formulaic praise used in this hadith three times to emphasize the divine origin of each statement
key_terms.علم: in this context: sign or standard that distinguishes between two opposing realities; Ali is the criterion that separates the believer from the hypocrite
key_terms.عيبة علمي: treasury of my knowledge; a chest or repository, signifying that Ali is entrusted with the Prophet's esoteric and exoteric knowledge
key_terms.منار الهدى: beacon/lighthouse of guidance; a metaphor for moral and spiritual direction
key_terms.وصي: legatee/designated successor; one explicitly appointed to inherit a position of authority
key_terms.ولاية: wilaya — guardianship, authority, and spiritual leadership; the Shia doctrinal concept of the Imam's divinely-sanctioned authority over the Muslim community

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the wilaya and imamate of Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This hadith records the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) publicly declaring the divine appointment of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) as his successor, guardian, and Imam over the Muslim community. Speaking directly to his companions, the Prophet frames wilaya (guardianship) over Ali as a divine commandment, and establishes Ali as the criterion between true faith and hypocrisy. The Prophet's closing statement — complaining to God about those who will oppress Ali — was understood by early Shia Muslims as a prophecy of the usurpation of Ali's rightful leadership after the Prophet's death, a foundational grievance in Shia historical consciousness.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Salama b. al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Abu’l Tahir Muhammad b. Tasnim al-Warraq narrated to us from `Abd al-Rahman b. Kathir from his father from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) said to his companions one day: O my companions!

Surely, Allah orders you to the wilaya of `Ali b. Abi Talib and to follow his example, for he is your master and your Imam after me. Do not dispute him, for you will have disbelieved; and do not split away from him, for you will have become misguided. Surely, Allah has made `Ali a sign [distinguishing] between faith and hypocrisy, for whoever loves him is a believer, and whoever hates him is a hypocrite.

Surely, Allah has made `Ali my deputy, the light post of guidance after me, the place of my secret, the repository of my knowledge, and my vicegerent among my people. I complain to Allah about his oppressors from my Nation after me.
